rounds.text: Redington Ltd presents a compelling value opportunity, trading at a modest P/E of 16x alongside a high-confidence rules-based screen score of 95 out of 100 [E1, E59]. Fundamental momentum is robust, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 23% and a striking 42% growth in compounded profit over the same period [E17, E21]. Capital efficiency significantly outpaces broader sector benchmarks, evidenced by the company's 15.8% ROCE and 4.45% ROA compared to sector medians of 6.82% and 2.92% respectively [E8, E10]. Furthermore, institutional conviction is strengthening as foreign institutions expanded their holdings to 63.42% in September 2026 from 56.99% in December 2023, driving positive institutional money flow [E41, E43]. Conceded: borrowings increased to Rs 2,842 Cr in March 2026, cash conversion sits at a weak 0.18x, and the historical peak-to-trough drawdown reaches a steep -80.2% [E34, E39, E52].

Despite recent headline earnings growth, severe cash generation and quality issues undermine Redington's financial stability, evidenced by a dismal cash conversion ratio of just 0.18x for March 2026 where reported profits far outpace actual operating cash flow [E34]. This divergence points directly to potential risks hidden in receivables or accruals [E34], and is further compounded by rising absolute borrowings which reached Rs 2,842 Cr in March 2026 [E39]. Valuation metrics also show signs of stretching, with the P/E of 18.78x and EV/EBITDA of 11.99x sitting above sector benchmarks of 18.5x and 10.54x respectively [E6, E11]. Furthermore, historical price performance highlights extreme structural volatility, demonstrated by a catastrophic worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -80.2% [E52]. Operating margins remain entirely stagnant at 2% with an inconsistent trend over recent periods [E30, E32], while domestic institutional holdings have simultaneously dwindled down to 16.01% [E42]. Conceded: [E44] the discounted cash flow model suggests a higher intrinsic value based on current projections.
